interpretation: The strict finite signs support seeking a theta-specific eventual positive-angle lemma; the degree-3 sign change rules out a same-sign claim starting at every nontrivial rung. Indeterminate degrees reflect the width and conditioning of the archived interval boxes, not a certified zero or negative sign.
nonclaims: This finite certificate is not an all-degree lower bound for X_n.
It does not show that rho_n has a positive uniform lower bound.
Independent interval propagation can make the displayed rho enclosure wider than [-1,1] at high finite degrees even though exact Cauchy applies.
It does not prove the next pivot, Xi-Laguerre inequalities, or RH.
It reuses archived interval inputs and is not an independent recomputation of theta quadrature.
